# Setup (install packages, load data, preprocess)
```{r}
# install packages
library(tm)
library(wordcloud)
library(ggplot2)
library(RColorBrewer)

# load data
data1 <- read.csv("data/TADA_A1_set1.csv")
data2 <- read.csv("data/TADA_A1_set2.csv")
```

# 1: What are the date ranges for the two sets? What information is provided in the CSV files? What are the languages in which tweets have been posted? 
```{r}
# date ranges
data1$date <- as.Date(data1$date)
data2$date <- as.Date(data2$date)
cat("Dataset 1 date range: ", as.character(min(data1$date, na.rm=TRUE)), " to ", as.character(max(data1$date, na.rm=TRUE)))
cat("\nDataset 2 date range: ", as.character(min(data2$date, na.rm=TRUE)), " to ", as.character(max(data2$date, na.rm=TRUE)))

# info provided
cat("\n\nColumns: ")
cat(colnames(data1))

# languages
lang_counts <- as.data.frame(table(c(data1$lang, data2$lang)))
cat("\n\nTweet languages:")
sort(table(c(data1$lang, data2$lang)), decreasing = TRUE)
```

# 2: What is the total number of posts in set 1? What is the total in set 2? 
```{r}
cat("Number of posts in dataset 1: ", length(data1$id))
cat("\nNumber of posts in dataset 2: ", length(data2$id))
```

# preprocess texts
```{r}
data1_en <- data1[data1$lang == "en", ]
data2_en <- data2[data2$lang == "en", ]
length(data1_en$id)
length(data2_en$id)

corpus1 <- Corpus(VectorSource(data1_en$text))
corpus1 <- tm_map(corpus1, content_transformer(tolower))
corpus1 <- tm_map(corpus1, removePunctuation)
corpus1 <- tm_map(corpus1, removeNumbers)
corpus1 <- tm_map(corpus1, function(x) removeWords(x, stopwords("en")))
corpus1_text <- sapply(corpus1, as.character)

corpus2 <- Corpus(VectorSource(data2_en$text))
corpus2 <- tm_map(corpus2, content_transformer(tolower))
corpus2 <- tm_map(corpus2, removePunctuation)
corpus2 <- tm_map(corpus2, removeNumbers)
corpus2 <- tm_map(corpus2, function(x) removeWords(x, stopwords("en")))
corpus2_text <- sapply(corpus2, as.character)
```

# 3: How many tweets are there for methadone, Suboxone, and fentanyl in total? Tip: sometimes alternative expressions are used for substances (eg., fent for fentanyl)
```{r}
methadone_regex <- "(methadone)|(dolophine)|(methadose)|(diskets)"
suboxone_regex <- "(suboxone)|(buprenorphine[- /]naloxone)"
fentanyl_regex <- "fent"

methadone1 <- Corpus(VectorSource(corpus1_text[grepl(methadone_regex, corpus1_text)]))
methadone2 <- Corpus(VectorSource(corpus2_text[grepl(methadone_regex, corpus2_text)]))
suboxone1 <- Corpus(VectorSource(corpus1_text[grepl(suboxone_regex, corpus1_text)]))
suboxone2 <- Corpus(VectorSource(corpus2_text[grepl(suboxone_regex, corpus2_text)]))
fentanyl1 <- Corpus(VectorSource(corpus1_text[grepl(fentanyl_regex, corpus1_text)]))
fentanyl2 <- Corpus(VectorSource(corpus2_text[grepl(fentanyl_regex, corpus2_text)]))

cat("Methadone posts in set 1: ", length(methadone1))
cat("\nMethadone posts in set 2: ", length(methadone2))
cat("\nSuboxone posts in set 1: ", length(suboxone1))
cat("\nSuboxone posts in set 2: ", length(suboxone2))
cat("\nFentanyl posts in set 1: ", length(fentanyl1))
cat("\nFentanyl posts in set 2: ", length(fentanyl2))
```

# 4: Are there fentanyl analogs that are also being discussed (eg., carfentanil)?
```{r}
cat("Number of tweets:\n")
analog_list <- list("carfentanil", "acetylfentanyl", "furanylfentanyl", "butyrylfentanyl", "acrylfentanyl", "methylfentanyl")
for (analog in analog_list) {
  count <- sum(grepl(analog, sapply(corpus1, as.character))) + sum(grepl(analog, sapply(corpus2, as.character)))
  cat(" ", analog, count, "\n")
}
```

# 5: What are some of the topics that are most closely associated with each of the three substances? The top 5-10 topics (if relevant) are acceptable.
```{r}
# stem
corpus1 <- tm_map(corpus1, stemDocument)
corpus2 <- tm_map(corpus2, stemDocument)

# create document term matrices
dtm1 <- DocumentTermMatrix(corpus1)
dtm2 <- DocumentTermMatrix(corpus2)

print("Methadone topics in set 1:")
print(head(sort(unlist(findAssocs(dtm1, "methadon", 0)), decreasing = TRUE), 10))
print("Methadone topics in set 2:")
print(head(sort(unlist(findAssocs(dtm2, "methadon", 0)), decreasing = TRUE), 10))

print("Suboxone topics in set 1:")
print(head(sort(unlist(findAssocs(dtm1, "suboxon", 0)), decreasing = TRUE), 10))
print("Suboxone topics in set 2:")
print(head(sort(unlist(findAssocs(dtm2, "suboxon", 0)), decreasing = TRUE), 10))

print("Fentanyl topics in set 1:")
print(head(sort(unlist(findAssocs(dtm1, "fentanyl", 0)), decreasing = TRUE), 10))
print("Fentanyl topics in set 2:")
print(head(sort(unlist(findAssocs(dtm2, "fentanyl", 0)), decreasing = TRUE), 10))

```

# 7: Generate appropriate figures to compare how the frequencies of mentions of these substances differ.
```{r}
all_dates <- c(data1_en$date, data2_en$date)
all_text <- tolower(as.character(c(data1_en$text, data2_en$text)))

week <- c(
  as.Date("2019-11-01") + 7 * floor(as.numeric(data1_en$date - as.Date("2019-11-01")) / 7),
  as.Date("2020-02-01") + 7 * floor(as.numeric(data2_en$date - as.Date("2020-02-01")) / 7)
)

mentions <- data.frame(week = week, Methadone = grepl(methadone_regex, all_text),
  Suboxone = grepl(suboxone_regex, all_text), Fentanyl = grepl(fentanyl_regex, all_text))

weekly_counts <- aggregate(. ~ week, data = mentions, FUN = sum)
weekly_counts <- weekly_counts[order(weekly_counts$week), ]

plot_data <- data.frame(
  week = rep(weekly_counts$week, 3),
  substance = rep(c("Methadone", "Suboxone", "Fentanyl"), each = nrow(weekly_counts)),
  posts = c(weekly_counts$Methadone, weekly_counts$Suboxone, weekly_counts$Fentanyl)
)

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = week, y = posts, color = substance)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = as.Date("2020-02-01"), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Substance Mentions Over Time", x = "Date", y = "Posts per Week (log scale)", color = "Substance") +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 weeks", date_labels = "%b %d") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "top")

counts <- rbind(
  data.frame(Dataset = "Dataset 1", Substance = c("Methadone", "Suboxone", "Fentanyl"),
             Posts = c(length(methadone1), length(suboxone1), length(fentanyl1))),
  data.frame(Dataset = "Dataset 2", Substance = c("Methadone", "Suboxone", "Fentanyl"),
             Posts = c(length(methadone2), length(suboxone2), length(fentanyl2))))

ggplot(counts, aes(x = Substance, y = Posts, fill = Dataset)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(title = "Substance Mentions by Dataset", x = "Substance", y = "Number of Posts (log scale)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 8: Find the top 10 most frequent bigrams in each of the three sets. Plot a bar chart for these.
```{r}
BigramTokenizer <- function(x) {
  unlist(lapply(ngrams(words(x), 2), paste, collapse = " "), use.names = FALSE)
}
get_top10_bigrams <- function(corpus) {
  bigram_counts <- table(unlist(lapply(corpus, function(x) BigramTokenizer(as.character(x)))))
  head(sort(bigram_counts, decreasing = TRUE), 10)
}
corpora <- list(methadone1 = methadone1, methadone2 = methadone2, suboxone1 = suboxone1,
                suboxone2 = suboxone2, fentanyl1 = fentanyl1, fentanyl2 = fentanyl2)
for (name in names(corpora)) {
  bigram10 <- get_top10_bigrams(corpora[[name]])
  cat("Top 10 bigrams for", name, ":\n")
  for (i in seq_along(bigram10)) {
    cat("  ", names(bigram10)[i], ":", bigram10[i], "\n")
  }
}

# plot
for (name in names(corpora)) {
  bigram10 <- get_top10_bigrams(corpora[[name]])
  plot_data <- data.frame(
    bigram = names(bigram10),
    frequency = as.numeric(bigram10)
  )
  plot_data$bigram <- factor(plot_data$bigram, levels = plot_data$bigram[order(plot_data$frequency)])
  print(
    ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = bigram, y = frequency)) 
    + geom_col(fill = "cornflowerblue") 
    + coord_flip() 
    + labs(title = paste("Top 10 Bigrams:", name), x = "Bigram", y = "Frequency") 
    # + theme_minimal()
    + theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"), 
            axis.title = element_text(size = 16), axis.text = element_text(size = 14))
  )
}
```
